I'm a bit biased on this review as I do the voice acting for the father over the phone. But here me out. This game... is incredible. Yes yes yes, the sound design, the scares, the liminal spaces, and the lighting are all phenomenal and every horror dev should take notes. Yes yes yes, as far as anomaly games this one stands out as one of the best!! BUT THE STORY steals the entire spotlight. Since I voiced one of the characters there was a huge chunk of the story I was aware of going in, but seeing the execution was nothing short of brilliant. If you're someone who appreciates story first and foremost in your horror games you'll be pleased to know that Captured 2 delivers and uses many elements in it's story telling: audio recordings, tv and radio broadcast, and even the environment itself help to further the story along. And the ending, was just so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. I was in tears. I hope when anyone plays Captured 2 they see more than just a horror game, but something that was created with passion every step of the way. So many hands were involved with it's creation, each one pouring their heart into their role, and I just think the final result will be talked about for years to come.

Incorrect Labeling on Anomalies ruins this game heavily. Edit: Spoke with the Dev on stream about this and it seems to be a common thing on the genre of Anomaly Hunting games. Common thing to have the Anomaly Counter 0'd immediately when you guess wrong on these kinds of events. The only anomaly game that has had this was Hospital 666 on Steam where making one mistake would take you down to floor 0. I sadly don't like that aspect from these games and truly the reason why I review this is because I was enjoying the game a lot, it's quite the gem when it comes to playing it and there's mechanics beyond just anomaly hunting which is appreciated. However, the punishment for missing one anomaly means you lose all your stacks of anomalies as for example in my game 8/13 to 0/13... It doesn't feel good and it just extends the game in a rather bothersome way. I feel like the punishment of dying should be the only one that resets your anomalies found to 0 instead of missing out on an anomaly that you didn't see. The developer has offered me to play on Story Mode as that would lower the Anomaly lost by 50% but... To me it feels like it just shouldn't be like that period, just going through rooms while missing anomalies feels like shouldn't punish the player at all and it should only punish whenever the player it taken out by the actual monsters. All in all, scary game but I guess I should have decided to switch to Story Mode instead of playing Normal Difficulty. Maybe someday I'll get back to this one but for now it's a pass it has ruined my mood sadly.

One of the monsters in the game, that supposedly triggers off the sound of your voice through your microphone, actually triggers from ANY sound that goes into the microphone including the game's own sound from the speakers. This makes it so that the monster immediately triggers and kills you as soon as they appear, as their appearance has a loud music that's meant to scare you, but the music itself triggers the monster and it kills you immediately. No amount of sneaking, being quiet, or anything avoids this, and it completely defeats the point of the monster and makes the game unplayable. Asking for help in the support forum the developer unfortunately either didn't understand the issue or was unwilling to help, just replied with "You have to sneak!" So no help there unfortunately. Can't recommend the game while it is in that state as it's pointless to play with this bug. UPDATE: We ended up disabling and disconnecting the microphone from the computer and from that point Walk-E became extremely easy not only to avoid but to manipulate, easily leading him on by standing up and crouching around the study desk to get by when he was blocking the hallway. So the issue described above was 100% correct, the game does present the issue of triggering itself through its own sound, and was completely solved by removing the mic. In the end, the game was fun and the message at the end was sweet so I've changed the review to Recommended because I do recommend it all things considered. To the developer's response below: It was 100% the monster's own sounds being picked up through the mic from the speakers that was triggering it, it was not in any way "footsteps", and this was clearly and obviously visible in the clips I showed. You made a good game, it does have this one issue that should not happen, a sound-triggered monster should not trigger off of its own sounds. It just shouldn't happen. But the game is good anyway, you don't need to be defensive about it, just try to fix it if you can, and if you can't, at least don't deny when it happens to people.

I have very little-nothing issue wise with the game. The message is brilliant and one that is kinda overlooked / not really thought about much, but bringing it up is not a bad thing at all. The game is good, the story is well thought out and the lore you learn about through some of the larger rooms, that have the monster dolls in, is really interesting and how it's laid out is clear and leaves you piecing things together. Monster designs are solid and the behaviours hit well. I don't normally physically jump to jump scares, in this game I have done repeatedly. Got used to Ring-Ring's locations, but there are times where its appearance is unexpected for how soon or late it appeared. His sound is enough to get your heart pounding. Head turning for Carrocteras is very smooth, which does add quite a bit of an unease factor to what is still the most unnerving character, Walk-e has it's own unease factor that is done well also... But Carroteras does it better. Only complaints I have is the very occasional lag spike when opening the laundry room door, that seems to push you back slightly, and when a couple of the larger room deformation anomaly appear on a loop. Overall the game is solid and is pretty good for its jump scares, a big improvement compared to the 1st and it does make me wonder if there could be a 3rd game planned, or an entirely different game done with a similar style.

When you think about the concept of a sequel, it's often something of a pipe dream for that sequel to not only recapture the quality of what came before, but for it to improve upon its concepts. Though, not all sequels often have all that much to follow up, which is the case for Captured 2. The first game, suitably titled: Captured, was a simple, but enjoyable Skinamarinkesque spot-the-anomaly game. In fact, the way I've talked about it downplays its qualities as I personally felt it was the best of its type. I appreciated the P.T. style looping hallway and I felt the anomalies were fun to spot, and at times even funny in their own right. I also liked how the game parceled out its story, giving it to you through anomalous TVs and phones that let you hear of the world outside of your hell. In that way, I think the game tries to explore a bit the concept behind Skinamarink rather than just showing off what it'd be like to experience it yourself, which is the final positive quality about the first. Captured 2, in two major ways, improves upon the first. For one, the gameplay loop is just across the board better. There's little bits of improvement in terms of enemy interaction, anomalies generally felt more interesting and impactful due to their relevancy to the plot, and there was a bit more humor in the game on the anomaly front as well. You get this little tale between toilets and chairs, one I mustn't spoil, but it's a great gag that surprisingly does not ruin the atmosphere of the game at all. Secondarily, there's an actual plot now beyond the simple "you're in a loop, your recordings make it out, and your family misses you." Honestly, I was impressed by the game in this respect. As I took note of previously, certain anomalies exist as extensions of the story. Your loops also change throughout the days as a response to the story. As such, you feel a lot more connected to your characters and what is happening, which is a great little touch. I think the tragedy of this character being separated from her family and forgetting even their worst memories associated with her family, namely the loss of her mother, is a well done one. I cannot say it moved me especially, but I felt that it was quite well done for the few hours the game ends up lasting. The closing scene felt like a sweet way to close what ends up being a fairly well-paced, brisk experience. On the other hand, the final message that the developer leaves off with almost made me tear up. It completely recontextualizes the game as being an exploration of the horrors of Alzheimer's and what it could be like to live day by day and begin to lose your memories permanently. I won't get too deep into it because I don't like the idea of talking about something so personal as that in an interview, but I can say it makes the game feel more impactful to me to have that context behind it. I would not say this is a flawless instance of what this series could do, but outside of gameplay I do not know really where they could go next as the game feels pretty final in that regard. Mainly, I think the enemies, just as they were in the first, are somewhat of a disappointment mechanically. The first game was generally fairly simple with its enemies, but they added a nice bit of active horror to the experience that kept' you on your toes. Here, the enemies don't feel significantly different from the experience of the first, and in fact they feel somewhat unbalanced in the normal mode. Mainly, I see no reason for Jestie's existence as it asks for the same response that Ring-A-Ding does. Walk-E was easily the best of the enemies as it actually tangibly affected my gameplay in the long-term (as long as any given loop can be, that is). It was also great fun because I streamed this game to a friend in discord, which added another layer to the whole thing. Nevertheless, this is no great slight against the game. As is, I think the enemies serve as much purpose as they do in the first game, which is to say they act as little more than mood enhancers that sometimes impact your gameplay. For me, that's enough. I'm more than excited to see what the developer goes on to do next after this. Having the willingness to go back and improve on an idea and actually succeed in doing so is an impressive thing to me, and I also love that they took what could have just been a fun idea and nothing more and injected something personal into it, making it feel so much more substantial than it otherwise would feel.

One of the best horror experiences of this year, seriously state of the art. I'm usually not into anomaly detection games and don't write many reviews, but I made an exception for Captured and Captured 2 because they're just that good at rising tension. No dumb jumpscares, those are very well timed and even then the scariest moments are all very subtle and actually creeped me out every time. Very good graphics and atmosphere, anomalies are unique enough not too repeat too frequently and some of them have bigger locations to explore. Seriously, do yourself a favor and get this if you're into any kind of horror, on top of all these things there's a genuinely great story too that moved me to tears at the end. 10/10.

I screamed. A lot. Normally I don't. This game made me scream. Constantly. The scares were fair and the story was beautiful at the end. I believe this was the first horror game where I cried at once it was all finished. Imagine PT, but as a game with objectives where you have to suddenly identify what's changed in specific rooms. Some changes are extremely easy to spot as you run to room to room. Others? Not so much. Even when you think you have a room perfectly memorized. You go through thinking you nailed it only to see you had missed a subtle detail. The monsters are incredible well done, the sound is perfect, and the gameplay is a solid 12/10. I had zero issues when playing and I really, really enjoyed this gem! I would play it and scream again.

While a pretty short horror game, this game for it's price is heavily worth it and hell, I would say it's worth even more in my book. The game has beautiful graphics and for a observation duty style like game I was not expecting an actual good story, but the story is pretty good and it's not really in depth. It might be somewhat basic, but the developer manages to make it seem more than basic based on the events happening around you. Every level/day the main area changes subtlety but manages to keep that lore/plot there to really indicate everything in the world is changing while you are gone. "Captured". Now don't get me started about the monsters. Every monster that I have encountered has genuinely made me jump, just from getting too focused on looking for anomalies. I have never been jump scared the amount of times this game has and that is genuinely impressive as I've have been playing horror games for many years. Lastly, the only complaint I had about the game personally was the lack of battery spawns, you need batteries in order to scan for anomalies, etc, and well if none spawn you're out of luck and have to go next restarting your counter. It may just be a skill issue, which it probably is, but it did bother me nonetheless. Another thing that was an issue was the doors, now I love dragging door mechanics, but in this game the doors are rather scuffy especially while attempting to close them. Thankfully, the developer already thought of that and managed to add a easy door accessibility option so that worry wasn't happening anymore. Anyways, this game is truly a hidden gem I highly recommend!
